Climate Policy Crossroads

Greenpeace and Friends of the Earth have warned Prime Minister Andy Burnham that the government risks failing its net zero targets by treating major infrastructure and energy decisions in isolation. A joint letter highlights that approvals for the Rosebank oilfield, Heathrow airport expansion, adjusted electric vehicle targets, and potential cuts to heat pump grants could collectively produce 402 million tonnes of CO2 over 25 years.

Impact and Oversight

Campaigners argue this cumulative emissions profile undermines the UK's carbon budgets. While the government maintains that reindustrialization will not compromise climate obligations, critics suggest that fragmented departmental decisions mask the long-term environmental and economic costs. Readers can track the government’s forthcoming policy announcements and official climate progress reports via the source documentation provided.
